paper.title: Distributed Learning in Multi-Armed Bandit with Multiple Players

settings.name_in_paper: Decentralized MAB with M distributed players (collision models 1 and 2)
unmapped: M < N distributed players, no communication; each player observes only its own arm and collisions
Collision model 1: colliding players share reward (one gets it); collision model 2: no one gets reward
Regret is system regret against the M best arms (centralized known-model benchmark)
Single-parameter reward family satisfying Lai-Robbins regularity conditions C1-C4 (and C5 for estimators)
M best arms have distinct nonnegative means
Players know the number of players M
settings.definition_quote: There are $M$ distributed players competing for $N$ independent arms. Each arm, when played, offers i.i.d. reward according to a distribution with an unknown parameter. At each time, each player chooses one arm to play without exchanging observations or any information with other players. Players choosing the same arm collide, and, depending on the collision model, either no one receives reward or the colliding players share the reward in an arbitrary way.

algorithms.name: Decentralized TDFS policy pi*_F (with pre-agreement), built on Lai-Robbins policy
Decentralized TDFS policy pi*_F without pre-agreement (random offsets)

symbols.L_Theta: instance-dependent constant; per the proof, the centralized Anantharam et al. constant sum_{j: mu_j < mu_sigma(M)} (mu_sigma(M) - mu_j)/I(theta_j, theta_sigma(M))

conditions: M best arms have nonnegative means

source.label: thm:optorder
source.quote: Under both collision models, the optimal order of the system regret growth rate of the decentralized MAB is logarithmic, \ie for an optimal decentralized policy $\pi^*$, we have L(\Theta)\le\liminf_{T\rightarrow\infty}\frac{R_T^{\pi^*}(\Theta)}{\log T}\le\limsup_{T\rightarrow\infty}\frac{R_T^{\pi^*}(\Theta)}{\log T}\le U(\Theta) for some constants $L(\Theta)$ and $U(\Theta)$ that depend on $\Theta$.

results.notes: Theorem states only existence of constant L(Theta); proof identifies it with the centralized lower bound (eqn cenlow) via Lemma 1. Regret defined via means of reward Y(t) in expectation -> pseudo_regret.

symbols.C_Theta_1: M*(sum_{i=1}^M x_i mu_sigma(i) - sum_{n: mu_n < mu_sigma(M)} mu_n / I(theta_n, theta_sigma(M)))

conditions: M best arms have distinct nonnegative means
tuning: Lai-Robbins point estimates and confidence bounds satisfying C5

source.label: thm:worstcase
source.quote: Under the TDFS policy $\pi^*_F$, we have, for some constant $C(\Theta)$, \limsup_{T\rightarrow\infty}\frac{R^{\pi^*_F}_T(\Theta)}{\log T}\le C(\Theta). ... Under collision model 1, C(\Theta)=M(\Sigma_{i=1}^Mx_k\mu(\theta_{\sigma(i)})-\Sigma_{n:\mu(\theta_n)<\mu(\theta_{\sigma(M)})}\frac{\mu(\theta_{n})}{I(\theta_{n},\theta_{\sigma(M)})}).

results.notes: Paper writes x_k inside sum over i (typo for x_i, per Appendix E). Theorem 1 upper part (U(Theta)) is established by this result.

symbols.C_Theta_2: M*(sum_{i=1}^M sum_{k=1}^M x_k mu_sigma(i) - sum_{n: mu_n < mu_sigma(M)} mu_n * max{1/I(theta_n,theta_sigma(M)) - sum_{i=1}^{M-1} 1/I(theta_n,theta_sigma(i)), 0})

conditions: M best arms have distinct nonnegative means
tuning: Lai-Robbins point estimates and confidence bounds satisfying C5
results.notes: Theorem 3 (fairness) states each player's local regret rate equals 1/M of the system rate; not recorded separately.

conditions: M best arms have distinct nonnegative means

source.label: thm:optElimPre
source.quote: The decentralized TDFS policy $\pi_F^*$ without pre-agreement is order-optimal and fair.

results.notes: 'Order-optimal' interpreted as limsup R_T/log T <= constant, as in Theorem 2; proof sketch in Appendix F.

symbols.L_TDS: sum_{i=1}^M sum_{j: mu_j < mu_sigma(M)} (mu_sigma(M) - mu_j)/I(theta_j, theta_sigma(i))

conditions: policy is uniformly good and in the Time Division Selection (TDS) class

source.label: thm:lowerboundTDS
source.quote: For any uniformly good decentralized policy $\pi$ in the TDS class, we have \liminf_{T\rightarrow\infty}\frac{R_T^{\pi}(\Theta)}{\log T}\ge\Sigma_{i=1}^M\Sigma_{j:\mu(\theta_j)<\mu(\theta_{\sigma(M)})}\frac{\mu(\theta_{\sigma(M)})-\mu(\theta_{j})}{I(\theta_{j},\theta_{\sigma(i)})}.

results.notes: Algorithm class: uniformly good TDS policies (fixed Theta-independent time shares of the M best arms).
